stories.title: Van Assche Wins Estoril — First ATP Title at 22
stories.angle: FOLLOW-UP — Luca Van Assche (FRA, 22) defeated Alexander Blockx (BEL, 21) 6-4, 4-6, 7-5 in the Millennium Estoril Open final on Sunday July 26 to claim his first ATP Tour title. Van Assche entered the week ranked No. 65; he rises to a new career high of No. 48 — his first time in the top 50. The match lasted 2 hours and 24 minutes. Blockx, 21, from Antwerp, was the 2023 Australian Open boys champion and reached a career high of No. 36 in May 2026 (after reaching the Madrid Masters 1000 semifinals). Both players were competing in their first ATP final. Van Assche had beaten top seed Rublev in the QF (covered July 25). He is now the youngest Frenchman with an ATP clay title in the current era.

stories.title: Korpatsch Wins Hamburg — First German Champion Since Steffi Graf in 1992
stories.angle: FOLLOW-UP — Tamara Korpatsch (GER, 31, wildcard) defeated Anna Bondar (HUN) 6-3, 6-3 in the MSC Hamburg Ladies Open (WTA 500) final on Sunday July 26. Korpatsch won in 1 hour and 28 minutes — on home clay in her hometown of Hamburg. She became the first German player to win the Hamburg title since Steffi Graf in 1992, a gap of 34 years. Graf had won six consecutive Hamburg titles from 1987–1992. Korpatsch entered the week ranked approximately No. 95; the title takes her into the WTA top 50 for the first time in her career (previous best: No. 71 in October 2023). This is her second career WTA title (first: 2023 Transylvania Open). Her career record vs. Bondar is now 5-0.

stories.title: Tagger Wins Prague — First WTA Title at 18, Youngest in Top 50
stories.angle: FOLLOW-UP — Lilli Tagger (AUT, 18) defeated Daria Snigur (UKR, No. 8 seed) 7-6(3), 6-2 in the Livesport Prague Open (WTA 250) final on Sunday July 26 to claim her first WTA Tour singles title. Tagger, born February 17, 2008, is now the youngest player in the WTA top 50 (approximately No. 45). She is only the second teenager — after Mirra Andreeva — to win a WTA singles title in 2026. Tagger trained at the Francesca Schiavone Academy in Varese, Italy, and won the 2025 French Open girls' title before turning professional. She plays with a one-handed backhand, highly unusual on the WTA Tour. In the final, Snigur built a 5-2 lead in the first set before Tagger leveled at 5-5 and won the tiebreak 7-3, then ran out the second set 6-2.

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Lilli Tagger is 18 years old. 🌟

She was down 2-5 in the first set of her first WTA final.

She won the next five games. Then the tiebreak. Then the second set 6-2.

Austria's newest champion. Youngest player in the WTA top 50.

#Tennis #WTAPrague #WTA

stories.title: Canadian Open Updates — Wild Cards, Mboko Out, Draws Friday
stories.angle: FOLLOW-UP — Fresh developments in the buildup to the National Bank Open. Women's Toronto (Aug 1–11): Tennis Canada confirmed final wild cards — Carol Zhao (CAN, ranked No. 406, age 31) receives her final-season home farewell appearance; Ariana Arseneault (CAN, from Richmond Hill, Ontario) also receives a wild card. Victoria Mboko (CAN, No. 10, 19 years old, defending champion from 2025 Montreal) is out with a medial collateral ligament injury in her left knee, suffered in a match against Karolina Pliskova at the HSBC Championships in London. She has confirmed she will attend the tournament in person. Men's Montreal (Aug 4–13): Sinner (elbow), Djokovic (reduced schedule), and Alcaraz (wrist) all confirmed absent; Zverev likely top seed; Shelton defending; Auger-Aliassime in home field. Draws scheduled for July 31.

stories.title: DC Open Begins — North American Hard Court Swing Opens in Washington
stories.angle: NEW STORY — The Mubadala Citi DC Open (ATP 500 / WTA 500) opens today in Washington D.C. at the William H.G. FitzGerald Tennis Center, running July 27–August 2. This is the first hard court tournament of the North American summer swing. Key players in the men's draw: Taylor Fritz (3rd seed), Frances Tiafoe (hometown favorite). In the women's draw, Alex Eala (Philippines) enters at a new career high of No. 29 following a strong grass-court season. The DC Open serves as a last warm-up option before the Canadian Open (Aug 1/4) for players who chose Washington over the clay events that closed Sunday.
